stem.en: Fructose is sweeter than glucose, gram for gram, though they have the same atoms. Kabir says "so fructose has more sugar in it". What is the better reading?

text.en: Sweetness is not an amount of sugar; it is how well a molecule fits the tongue's detector. Fructose's shape fits better. Same atoms, different shape, different fit.

feedback.en: A gram of fructose and a gram of glucose are the same atoms in the same amount. The difference is arrangement.
Same formula. Six carbons, twelve hydrogens, six oxygens, in both.
The tongue is doing exactly its job: it reads shape. A different shape reads differently.

explanation.en: Isomers have the same atoms and different shapes. A detector that reads shape, which is what your tongue is, will read them differently.
